app.name: ITPMD Project Hub
app.description: LANDBANK ITPMD Project Hub (MVP): project schedules, issues, risks, financials and the monthly PSR approval cycle (PM > DH > conditional Sponsor), rolled up into a PSC portfolio view.

domain.summary: ITPMD Project Hub, MVP (Phase 1) scope only, per BRD v1.1 §4.3 and the orchestrator's scope decision. The domain centers on the monthly PSR cycle: a Project Manager builds and baselines a schedule, assigns activities to team members who update only their own work (My Tasks), tracks issues/risks/financials during the period, generates a Project Status Report from live data, and routes it PM -> Department Head -> (Project Sponsor, when the routing rule applies) for approval; approved PSRs lock as snapshots and roll up into a PSC portfolio view and Portfolio PSR. Deferred entirely (Phase 2/3, out of this build): Liquidated Damages, Change Requests, forecast validation/approval workflow and automatic forecast recalculation, MoM and Lessons Learned, Project Discussions, the LEAF AI assistant (Basic/Advanced/governance), SIEM/AD-LDAP integration, and the drag-and-drop Gantt. Platform-level NFRs that Kissflow provides natively or that are infra/ops concerns (password/lockout policy specifics, MFA mechanism, session timeout, HTTPS, SIEM transport, backup/DR) are noted as platform/not-authored and are not modeled as domain entities or rules.

personas.name: Project Manager (PM)
personas.description: ITPMD project manager who runs the day-to-day of an assigned IT project: schedule, issues, risks and financials, and prepares/submits the monthly PSR.
goals: One system of record for the project instead of scattered schedules, spreadsheets and documents (BRD §2.1, objective O1)
Cut PSR preparation time by generating the report from live system data instead of re-typing it (objective O2)
Get an early warning on schedule slippage and cost overruns before they become critical (objective O4)
pain_points: Project information today is spread across separate schedules, spreadsheets and documents (BRD §2.1)
Status reports are compiled by hand each period (BRD §2.1)
No systemic early warning today when a forecast passes the baseline or a budget/contingency threshold is crossed (BRD §2.1, objective O4)
personas.evidence: BRD §5 Stakeholders and User Roles (Project Manager row); §2.1; §2.2 O1/O2/O4

personas.name: Project Team Member / Responsible Person
personas.description: A team member assigned specific activities and/or action items; updates only the work assigned to them.
goals: See everything assigned to me, across every project I'm on, in one place (My Tasks) (ITPH-00258)
Update my own progress directly, without waiting on the PM to relay it (ITPH-00256)
pain_points: No single place today to see assigned work across projects (BRD §1.4 'My Tasks' definition implies the gap this closes)
Without a control, anyone could edit anyone else's activity; the business explicitly restricts this (BRD BR-15 / ITPH-00257)
personas.evidence: BRD §5 (Project Team Member / Responsible Person row); §8.14 (ITPH-00253–00259); BR-15

personas.name: Department Head (DH)
personas.description: Head of the unit that owns the project; reviews, approves or returns PSRs, limited to the projects under their own responsibility.
goals: Validate the accuracy and completeness of a project's status before it moves forward (ITPH-00114)
Controlled, fully traceable approvals with a complete history (objective O3)
pain_points: Approvals and their history are not consistently tracked in one system today, motivating objective O3 (all approvals in-system with full history)

personas.name: Project Sponsor (PS)
personas.description: Business sponsor who gives final approval on a PSR only when the PS routing rule requires it.
goals: See and approve only the PSRs that actually require sponsor sign-off, not every report (BR-10)
pain_points: There is no confirmed, consistent rule today for when sponsor approval is even needed (BRD §15 open question #3; BR-10 is explicitly 'proposed')

personas.name: PSC Member
personas.description: Project Steering Committee member with portfolio-wide oversight; views dashboards, critical risks/issues, and generates the Portfolio PSR (PPSR).
goals: Portfolio visibility without having to request ad-hoc reports (objective O5)
See at a glance which projects need management attention (BR-06)
pain_points: The PSC has limited cross-project visibility today (BRD §2.1)

personas.name: QA
personas.description: ITPMD quality assurance. The BRD's proposed access matrix (§5.1) gives QA create/edit access to the risk register, but QA's dedicated work described in the requirements -- the cross-project risk and lessons-learned repositories (ITPH-0052, ITPH-00112) -- is explicitly Phase 2. QA has no distinct MVP journey in this domain model (see open-questions.md); flagged rather than invented.
goals: Reuse past risks and lessons across projects instead of rediscovering them on every new project (BRD §2.1; ITPH-0052)
pain_points: Lessons learned and past risks are not reused across projects today (BRD §2.1)
personas.evidence: BRD §5 (QA row); §5.1 access matrix (Risk register column); ITPH-0052, ITPH-00112 (both Phase 2)

personas.name: BA / Application Administrator
personas.description: ITPMD system owner who maintains the working calendar and alert thresholds/recipients (and, later, LEAF settings -- Phase 2, out of this build).
goals: Change working-calendar and alert policy without needing a code change (ITPH-001, ITPH-003)
pain_points: Configuration parameters like holidays and thresholds are not centrally, self-service maintained today (implied by BRD §2.1's general 'spread across tools' finding and by ITPH-001/003 asking for admin-maintained config)

personas.name: System / Security Administrator
personas.description: IT operations/security staff who manage user accounts, roles, permissions, unlocks/resets and audit review.
goals: Every user's access matches their current responsibility and only their assigned projects, deny-all by default (ITPH-00225)
Every action in the system traceable to a responsible user (objective O6, ITPH-00147)
pain_points: Passing IT Security review and VAPT with a full audit trail before go-live is an explicit, hard MVP exit gate (BRD §4.5, objective O6)
personas.evidence: BRD §5 (System / Security Administrator row); §8.11 (ITPH-00135–00147); §4.5; objective O6

journeys.name: Set up a project from approved master data
journeys.trigger: A new IT project is approved / kicks off in ITPMD.
steps: PM creates the project record: code, name, business unit, portfolio, assigned DH/PS.
PM records the procurement/contract details: vendor, NOA/PO/NTP dates, contract value, expiry.
PM records the approved budget and the approved contingency fund.
PM sets up the initial project team (who is assigned to this project).
journeys.outcome: The project exists as the single source of truth that scheduling, financials and later PSRs all build on.
journeys.frequency: Once per project (edited as master data changes are approved).
success_criteria: Project appears correctly in the portfolio list (ITPH-00124)
Changes to approved master data flow through to later PSRs and project records automatically (BR-13)
journeys.evidence: BRD §6.1 (first two bullets); §12 (Project, Procurement/Contract entities); BR-13; ITPH-008

journeys.name: Build and baseline the project schedule
journeys.trigger: Project master data exists and the project is ready to be scheduled.
steps: PM creates, edits and deletes project activities (ITPH-004).
PM defines planned start/end dates for each activity (ITPH-005).
PM defines dependencies between activities (ITPH-006).
PM identifies and maintains project milestones (ITPH-007).
PM establishes the approved schedule baseline (ITPH-009).
PM generates and views the Gantt chart (ITPH-0024).
journeys.outcome: An approved, dependency-consistent schedule with a locked baseline that later progress is measured against.
journeys.frequency: Once at project start; revisited whenever a re-baseline is approved.
success_criteria: A baseline is established and stays fixed once approved (BRD §1.4 'Baseline' definition)
Every change to the schedule is captured in schedule history (ITPH-0014)

journeys.name: Assign and reassign activities to team members
journeys.trigger: The schedule is built, or work needs to be rebalanced across the team.
steps: PM assigns each activity and milestone to a responsible team member (ITPH-00253).
The assignee is notified (ITPH-00255).
PM reassigns an activity to another team member at any time; the change is recorded in schedule history (ITPH-00254).
PM (or team member) filters the schedule to just their own assigned activities (ITPH-00259).
journeys.outcome: Every activity has a single clear owner, and every reassignment is traceable.
journeys.frequency: Ongoing, throughout the life of the project.
success_criteria: Every open activity has an assignee
Reassignments are visible in schedule history, not silently overwritten

journeys.name: Track progress, actuals and forecast during the period
journeys.trigger: Work is underway during the reporting period.
steps: Assignees record % complete, actual start and actual finish for their own activities (ITPH-0010, ITPH-0011, ITPH-00256; see also journey J-11).
PM manually updates forecast start/finish dates when their assessment of progress changes (ITPH-0013).
PM views planned vs. actual schedules to spot variance (ITPH-0012, ITPH-0016).
PM is alerted when the forecast finish passes the baseline finish or a schedule-risk threshold (ITPH-0022).
journeys.outcome: The schedule reflects true current status, with schedule health computed and an early warning raised on slippage.
journeys.frequency: Continuous; at minimum before each monthly PSR is generated.
success_criteria: Schedule health (Green/Amber/Red) is computed per BR-03
An alert fires the moment forecast finish exceeds baseline finish
journeys.evidence: BRD §8.2 (ITPH-0010–0013, 0016, 0022); BR-03; BR-15. Note: automatic forecast recalculation (ITPH-0017) and forecast validation/approval (ITPH-0019–0021) are Phase 2 -- the MVP forecast is manually updated by the PM only.

journeys.name: Manage issues, action items and decisions
journeys.trigger: A problem, blocker or open question is identified during project execution.
steps: PM creates and maintains an issue: category, priority (ITPH-0031, 0032).
PM assigns an issue owner and a target resolution date (ITPH-0033, 0034).
PM records the actions required to resolve the issue and assigns action items to team members (ITPH-0035, 0036).
PM tracks action item status so overdue actions are visible (ITPH-0037).
PM records project decisions and their rationale (ITPH-0038).
The issue escalates automatically when Critical or overdue past the configured aging period (ITPH-0039, §6.3).
journeys.outcome: Issues are tracked to resolution or escalated, with owners and action items clearly assigned.
success_criteria: Critical or aged-overdue issues escalate and appear on the PSC view (ITPH-0040, BR-21)
Every action item has a status and an owner

journeys.name: Manage the project risk register
journeys.trigger: A potential threat to the project is identified.
steps: PM creates and maintains a risk register entry (ITPH-0041).
PM categorizes the risk (ITPH-0042).
PM assesses probability and impact; the overall risk rating is computed per BR-04 (ITPH-0043).
PM assigns a risk owner (ITPH-0044).
PM defines mitigation actions and a response strategy (ITPH-0045, 0046).
PM monitors residual risk after mitigation (ITPH-0047).
The risk escalates automatically when rated High or Critical (ITPH-0048, §6.3).
PM maintains risk history/status over time (ITPH-0050).
journeys.outcome: Every risk has a current rating, an owner and a mitigation plan; High/Critical risks are visible to governance.
journeys.frequency: Ongoing, as risks are identified or reassessed.
success_criteria: Risk rating always follows the 5x5 probability x impact matrix (BR-04)
High/Critical risks appear on the PSC view (ITPH-0049)

journeys.name: Manage project financials
journeys.trigger: A budget is approved for the project, or costs/invoices are incurred during execution.
steps: PM records the approved project budget (ITPH-0053).
PM records approved changes to the budget with amount, effective date and reason (ITPH-0054); views the current approved budget after changes (ITPH-0055).
PM records the approved contingency fund (ITPH-0056) and monitors its utilization (ITPH-0065) and remaining balance (ITPH-0066).
PM records invoices with invoice/DO number and date, vendor, date paid, status and remarks (ITPH-0057).
PM records actual and committed project costs (ITPH-0058, 0059).
PM compares approved budget, actual cost, committed cost and forecast cost to spot variances (ITPH-0062); views the remaining budget/forecast balance (ITPH-0064).
journeys.outcome: An up-to-date financial position that feeds cost health (BR-05) and the PSR's financial summary.
journeys.frequency: Ongoing; reconciled at least once per reporting period.
success_criteria: Budget vs actual vs committed vs forecast reconciles for the PSR (ITPH-0068, 0069)
Cost health (Green/Amber/Red) is computed per BR-05
journeys.evidence: BRD §8.5 (ITPH-0053–0059, 0062, 0064, 0068, 0069); BR-05. Note: reforecasting workflow, variance-reason capture and vendor man-day rates (ITPH-0060, 0061, 0063, 0072) are Phase 2.

journeys.name: Generate, preview and submit the monthly PSR
journeys.trigger: The monthly reporting period deadline is approaching (PSR due working day 5 of the next month, BR-11).
steps: The Hub reminds the PM before the deadline (ITPH-00148, BR-11).
PM generates the PSR; static and computed sections (schedule, milestone, issue, risk, financial, action data) auto-populate from live data (ITPH-0094, 0095, 0027–0029).
PM adds a narrative update (ITPH-0096) and defines/confirms the reporting period (ITPH-0097).
PM attaches supporting documents (ITPH-0098).
PM identifies activities behind/ahead of schedule and milestones missed or forecast to be missed (ITPH-0106–0108), and plans the next period's activities/milestones (ITPH-0104).
PM previews the PSR before submission (ITPH-0099) and submits it to the DH (ITPH-00113).
journeys.outcome: A complete, accurate PSR -- built from system data, not re-typed -- submitted for approval on time.
success_criteria: PSR is submitted by the working-day-5 deadline (BR-11)
Auto-populated static fields match approved project master data and are never edited on an approved PSR (BR-13)

journeys.name: Revise and resubmit a returned PSR
journeys.trigger: The DH (or PS) returns the PSR with comments.
steps: PM is notified that the PSR was returned (ITPH-00121).
PM reviews the mandatory comments explaining what needs correction (ITPH-00116, BR-25).
PM revises the PSR.
PM resubmits the PSR for approval (ITPH-00117).
journeys.outcome: A corrected PSR re-enters the approval flow; nothing is lost from the original submission.
journeys.frequency: As needed, once per return cycle.
success_criteria: The full return -> revise -> resubmit history is retained and auditable (ITPH-00146)

journeys.name: Monitor schedule performance via the S-curve
journeys.trigger: Any time during execution, especially while preparing the PSR narrative.
steps: PM views the cumulative planned vs actual vs forecast S-curve for the project (ITPH-00266).
PM sees planned % to date, actual % to date, variance in percentage points and SPI (ITPH-00267).
PM hovers over the curve for exact weekly values, or views the same data as a table (ITPH-00268).
The S-curve is included when the PSR is generated (ITPH-00269).
journeys.outcome: Schedule performance trend is visible at a glance, quantified with SPI, and carried into the PSR.
journeys.frequency: Ongoing; at minimum, each time a PSR is generated.
success_criteria: S-curve points are computed per BR-17 (weekly, weighted by activity duration, planned from baseline / actual from actuals / forecast from today to forecast finish)

journeys.name: Work my assigned tasks (My Tasks)
journeys.trigger: An activity or action item is assigned to me.
steps: I receive a notification that an activity has been assigned to me (ITPH-00255).
I see it on my My Tasks page, alongside every other open activity and action item assigned to me across all my projects, with status and due dates (ITPH-00258).
I update % complete, actual start and actual finish for MY OWN activities only (ITPH-00256).
If I try to edit an activity that is not assigned to me, I am blocked (ITPH-00257).
I can filter the schedule view to show only my own assigned activities (ITPH-00259).
journeys.outcome: My work is visible and updatable from one place, without my being able to touch anyone else's schedule items.
success_criteria: Entering % complete > 0 sets the actual start if blank; entering 100% sets the actual finish to today (BR-15)
An assignee can never edit an activity not assigned to them (BR-15, ITPH-00257)

journeys.name: Review and approve/return a PSR
journeys.trigger: A PM submits a PSR (status moves to Submitted -- For DH Review).
steps: DH is notified that a PSR requires approval (ITPH-00149).
DH reviews the submitted PSR's schedule, issue, risk, financial and action content (ITPH-00114).
DH approves the PSR, or returns it with mandatory comments (ITPH-00115, 00116, BR-25).
If approved, the system checks the PS routing rule (BR-10) and either routes the PSR to the PS or finalizes it.
DH can view the PSR's approval status and full history at any time (ITPH-00120, 00123).
journeys.outcome: Only validated PSRs advance; every return carries an actionable, recorded comment.
journeys.frequency: Monthly, per project the DH is responsible for.
success_criteria: No PSR advances to Approved without an explicit DH action
A returned PSR always carries a comment (BR-25)

journeys.name: Approve a PSR requiring Sponsor sign-off
journeys.trigger: A DH-approved PSR meets the PS routing rule (BR-10: overall health Red, or a baseline/budget change is requested, or the project is flagged 'PS approval required').
steps: PS is notified of a PSR pending approval (ITPH-00157).
PS reviews the DH-approved PSR.
PS approves or returns the PSR (ITPH-00119).
journeys.outcome: The PSR receives the Bank's full governance sign-off, or is sent back for correction, per the routing rule.
journeys.frequency: Only for PSRs that meet the PS routing rule (not every monthly PSR).
success_criteria: PS only ever sees PSRs that actually meet BR-10's routing conditions

journeys.name: Monitor portfolio health and identify projects needing attention
journeys.trigger: Ongoing governance oversight, ad hoc or aligned to the monthly PSR cadence.
steps: PSC views all projects under the portfolio (ITPH-00124).
PSC filters projects by status, health, risk, business unit and other criteria (ITPH-00125).
PSC views dashboards of project status, risk, issue, milestone and financial performance (ITPH-00126).
PSC monitors project health indicators (ITPH-00132) and identifies projects requiring management attention per BR-06 (ITPH-00130).
PSC views critical issues and overdue actions (ITPH-0040), and high/critical risks (ITPH-0049).
journeys.outcome: The PSC directs its attention to the projects that need it, without requesting ad-hoc reports.
journeys.frequency: Continuous, aligned to the monthly PSR cycle.
success_criteria: 'Needs management attention' is computed consistently per BR-06 (overall Red, or any Critical risk/issue, or any overdue escalation)

journeys.name: Generate the Portfolio PSR (PPSR) and view PSR history
journeys.trigger: After the period's project PSRs have moved through approval.
steps: PSC views consolidated project status information across the portfolio (ITPH-00100).
PSC generates the Portfolio Project Status Report (PPSR) (ITPH-00101).
PSC (and PM) view historical PSRs to review performance and status trends over time (ITPH-00102).
PSC views the approval status of PSRs across the portfolio (ITPH-00122).
journeys.outcome: A consolidated, board-ready portfolio status report and a browsable PSR history.
journeys.frequency: Monthly, aligned to the PSR cycle.
success_criteria: The PPSR only rolls up PSRs that have reached Approved (locked snapshot), per BR-24

journeys.name: Configure the working calendar and alert settings
journeys.trigger: Onboarding, an announced holiday schedule, or a change in the Bank's threshold/escalation policy.
steps: Admin adds, edits or removes holidays and special non-working days, including dates and coverage (ITPH-001).
Admin configures alert thresholds, contract-expiration notification periods, aging periods and recipients for reminders and escalations (ITPH-003).
journeys.outcome: Schedule calculations (working-day logic) and escalation/reminder timing reflect current Bank policy without any code change.
journeys.frequency: Periodic (yearly holiday update; ad hoc threshold/policy changes).
success_criteria: Working-day-dependent calculations (durations, dependencies, forecasts, PSR deadline) respect the configured calendar (BR-01)

journeys.name: Administer users, roles and project access
journeys.trigger: Staff onboarding/offboarding or a change in someone's responsibilities.
steps: Admin creates and maintains user accounts (ITPH-00135).
Admin assigns users to appropriate roles (ITPH-00136).
Admin activates, deactivates or modifies user access (ITPH-00137).
Admin assigns users to specific projects, so each user can access only the projects relevant to their responsibilities (ITPH-00138); access defaults to deny-all otherwise (ITPH-00225).
Admin maintains role permissions centrally (ITPH-00145).
journeys.outcome: Every user's access matches their current responsibility and their current project assignments; no orphaned or over-privileged accounts.
journeys.frequency: Ongoing, as staffing or responsibilities change.
success_criteria: A user with no project assignment sees no project data (BR-23)

journeys.name: Review the audit trail
journeys.trigger: Periodic security/compliance review, or an investigation into a specific change.
steps: Admin views all system transactions and user actions recorded in the audit trail (ITPH-00147).
Admin (or any authorized user) traces a specific PSR's full lifecycle history -- creation, modification, submission, approval, return, comments, responsible users, timestamps (ITPH-00146).
journeys.outcome: Any change to project data, reports, approvals, configuration or access can be traced to the responsible user.
success_criteria: Every one of the confirmed audit log event types is captured (open question: the exact '7 identified log events' of ITPH-00213 are unconfirmed by LANDBANK -- see open-questions.md)
journeys.evidence: BRD §8.11 (ITPH-00146, 00147); §4.5 exit criteria; ITPH-00213; objective O6

entities.name: Project
entities.description: An IT project managed end-to-end in the Hub: master data, ownership and current health.
entities.lifecycle: Set up from approved master data -> active (scheduled, monitored, monthly PSR cycle) -> closed. Master data changes apply going forward only; approved PSRs already issued are never retroactively changed (BR-13).
relationships: a Project has one or more Procurement/Contract records
a Project has many Activities, Milestones, Dependencies and one active Baseline
a Project has many Issues, Risks, Budget Changes/Contingency Draws, Cost Entries and Invoices
a Project has many PSRs (one per reporting period)
a Project has many Project Assignments (its team)

entities.name: Procurement / Contract
entities.description: The procurement and contract record behind a project -- vendor and key procurement dates.
entities.lifecycle: Recorded at project set-up; procurement dates feed the schedule and contract-expiry information (the expiry ALERT itself is Phase 2, ITPH-00154).
relationships: belongs to a Project

entities.name: Activity
entities.description: A unit of scheduled work within a project's schedule.
entities.lifecycle: Created by the PM -> scheduled (planned dates, dependencies) -> baselined -> in progress (assignee updates % complete/actuals) -> forecast adjusted by PM as needed -> complete (100%, actual finish set). Only the PM can create, delete, move or re-baseline an activity; the assignee may only change their own activity's % complete and actual dates (BR-15).
relationships: belongs to a Project
may have a parent Activity (WBS hierarchy)
participates in Dependencies as predecessor and/or successor
has one current Activity Assignment (plus history)
a Milestone may reference an Activity it depends on or represent a deliverable date in its own right
entities.evidence: BRD §12 (Activity row); §8.2 (ITPH-004–0016); BR-15; BR-16 (drag rules noted as Phase 2, not modeled)

entities.name: Dependency
entities.description: A logical link between two activities in the same project's schedule.
entities.lifecycle: Defined by the PM when building the schedule; used to sequence activities and to prevent an activity from starting before its predecessors finish.
relationships: links two Activities within the same Project

entities.name: Milestone
entities.description: A key deliverable date in the project schedule.
entities.lifecycle: Identified by the PM during schedule build -> tracked against baseline date -> achieved, or flagged missed/forecast-late per BR-03.
relationships: belongs to a Project
entities.evidence: BRD §12 (Milestone row); §8.2 (ITPH-007); BR-03. Note: the 'price of deliverable' attribute in §12 exists solely to feed Liquidated Damages (Phase 2) and is dropped from this MVP entity.

entities.name: Baseline
entities.description: The approved, locked-in snapshot of a project's schedule (and budget) used to measure variance.
entities.lifecycle: Established once the PM's schedule is approved (ITPH-009); becomes the fixed reference for schedule/cost variance until a controlled re-baseline is approved.
relationships: belongs to a Project; a Project has one active Baseline at a time, and a history of prior baselines

entities.name: Issue
entities.description: A tracked problem affecting the project.
entities.lifecycle: Created and categorized by PM -> owner and target date assigned -> tracked -> escalates automatically when Critical or overdue past the aging period (BR-21) -> resolved/closed.
relationships: belongs to a Project
has many Action Items
may reference the Decision(s) that resolved it

entities.name: Action Item
entities.description: A follow-up action needed to resolve an issue (or, more broadly, a tracked to-do assigned to a team member).
entities.lifecycle: Recorded by PM as part of resolving an Issue -> assigned to a team member -> tracked to done, or flagged overdue and reminded (ITPH-00155).
relationships: typically belongs to an Issue, but can stand alone as a follow-up
assigned to a Team Member (Project Assignment) and surfaced on that member's My Tasks

entities.name: Decision
entities.description: A recorded project decision and its rationale.
entities.lifecycle: Recorded by the PM when a decision is made during project execution.
relationships: belongs to a Project
may reference the Issue it resolves

entities.name: Risk
entities.description: A potential threat to the project, tracked in the project's risk register.
entities.lifecycle: Created and categorized by PM -> probability/impact assessed, rating computed (BR-04) -> owner and mitigation/response assigned -> residual risk monitored -> escalates automatically when High/Critical (BR-22) -> status/history maintained over time.
relationships: belongs to a Project

entities.name: Budget Change / Contingency Draw
entities.description: An approved adjustment to the project's budget, or an approved draw against its contingency fund.
entities.lifecycle: Recorded by PM once approved; a budget change adjusts the project's current approved budget; a contingency draw reduces the available contingency balance.
relationships: belongs to a Project

entities.name: Cost Entry
entities.description: An actual, committed or forecast cost recorded against the project.
entities.lifecycle: Recorded by the PM as costs are incurred or committed; aggregated to produce the project's actual/committed/forecast totals used in cost health (BR-05) and the PSR financial summary.
relationships: belongs to a Project
may relate to an Invoice (an invoice's amount becomes an actual Cost Entry)

entities.name: Invoice
entities.description: A vendor invoice recorded against the project.
entities.lifecycle: Recorded by the PM as invoices are received/paid.
relationships: belongs to a Project

entities.name: Project Status Report (PSR)
entities.description: The monthly report of a project's schedule, milestone, issue, risk, financial and action status, routed for approval.
entities.lifecycle: Draft (PM, editable) -> Submitted -- For DH Review (locked) -> [Returned with mandatory comments -> Draft] -> DH Approved -- For PS Approval (only when BR-10's routing rule applies) -> Approved (final, read-only snapshot; rolls into the PPSR and PSR history). Per BR-13, an Approved PSR is never changed.
relationships: belongs to a Project; a Project accumulates a history of PSRs, one per reporting period

entities.name: Configuration
entities.description: App-wide administrative settings that drive schedule and escalation calculations.
key_attributes: issue/risk aging periods and escalation levels
entities.lifecycle: Maintained by the Application Administrator; changes take effect for future calculations.
relationships: referenced by every Project's schedule (working-day calculations, BR-01) and by every Issue/Risk's escalation logic (BR-21, BR-22)
entities.evidence: BRD §12 (Configuration row); §8.1 (ITPH-001, 003); BR-01. Note: LD rate/cap and password-policy parameters are excluded here -- LD is Phase 2, and password policy is a platform/not-authored NFR.

entities.name: Activity Assignment
entities.description: The record of who is (or was) responsible for a given activity.
entities.lifecycle: Created when the PM assigns an activity; superseded (with history preserved) each time the PM reassigns it.
relationships: an Activity has many Activity Assignments over time; the latest one is the current responsible person; feeds the assignee's My Tasks

entities.name: Notification
entities.description: An in-app (and emailed) alert to a user about an event relevant to them.
entities.lifecycle: Raised automatically by an event (assignment made, PSR routed for approval, threshold crossed, deadline approaching) and read/dismissed by the recipient.
relationships: issued to a User Account, in the context of a Project, Activity, Issue, Risk or PSR
entities.evidence: BRD §12 (Notification row); §8.12 (ITPH-00148–00155, 00157); §8.14 (ITPH-00255). Note: the 'mention' notification type belongs to Project Discussions (Phase 2) and is excluded here.

entities.name: User Account
entities.description: A person who logs into the Hub.
entities.lifecycle: Created and maintained by the System Administrator; activated, deactivated or modified as responsibilities change.
relationships: granted one or more Roles; linked to Projects via Project Assignment

entities.name: Project Assignment
entities.description: The link between a User Account and a Project, in a given role, that governs what that user can see and do on that project.
entities.lifecycle: Created by the System Administrator (or the PM, for team membership) when a user needs project access; the default is deny-all -- a user has no access to a project until assigned (BR-23).
relationships: links a User Account to a Project
entities.evidence: BRD §12 implied by §5.1's 'access to project data is further limited to assigned projects'; §8.11 (ITPH-00138, 00139); ITPH-00225; BR-23

entities.name: Audit Log Entry
entities.description: A record of a system transaction or user action, for traceability.
entities.lifecycle: Written automatically whenever a tracked action occurs across the Hub's MVP entities.
relationships: references the User Account that performed the action and the Project/PSR/entity it affected
entities.evidence: BRD §12 (User/Role/Permission/Audit log row); §8.11 (ITPH-00146, 00147); §4.5 exit criteria. Note: the exact set of the '7 identified log events' referenced by ITPH-00213 is unconfirmed by LANDBANK -- see open-questions.md.

business_rules.statement: Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and configured holidays. Activity durations, dependencies and forecasts all use working days.
business_rules.applies_to: Activity, Configuration / journeys J-02, J-04, J-16

business_rules.statement: Overall project completion % is the weighted average of leaf-activity % complete, weighted by planned duration. The PM may override with a recorded reason.

Schedule health variance = forecast finish minus baseline finish (working days). Green if variance <= 0; Amber if 1-10 days; Red if > 10 days or any missed milestone (a milestone past its baseline date and not yet achieved). A milestone that is only forecast late counts through the variance, not as missed.
business_rules.applies_to: Project, Activity, Milestone / journeys J-04, J-14
business_rules.evidence: BRD §7 BR-03; ITPH-0016, ITPH-0022. Uses the PM's manually-updated forecast (ITPH-0013, MVP) -- automatic forecast recalculation (ITPH-0017) is Phase 2.

business_rules.statement: Risk rating is 5x5 probability x impact score: 1-4 Low, 5-9 Medium, 10-16 High, 20-25 Critical. High and Critical risks escalate.
Cost health = forecast at completion divided by current approved budget. Green if <= 100%; Amber if > 100-105% or contingency use >= 75%; Red if > 105% or contingency exhausted.
business_rules.applies_to: Project, Cost Entry, Budget Change/Contingency Draw / journeys J-07, J-14
business_rules.evidence: BRD §7 BR-05; ITPH-0062. The threshold ALERT itself (ITPH-00152) is Phase 2; the health computation that budget/contingency tracking feeds is MVP.

business_rules.statement: Overall project health is the worst of schedule, cost, risk and issue health. 'Needs management attention' means overall Red, or any Critical risk/issue, or any overdue escalation.
A PSR routes to the Project Sponsor when any of: overall health is Red, a baseline or budget change is requested, or the project is flagged 'PS approval required'.
The PSR reporting period is monthly; the PSR is due on working day 5 of the following month. Reminders fire 3 days before, 1 day before, and on each overdue day.
Static PSR fields (project name, vendor, contract value, sponsor, dates) come from project master data. Changes to master data apply to later PSRs only; approved PSRs are never changed.
business_rules.applies_to: PSR, Project, Procurement/Contract / journeys J-01, J-08, J-09

business_rules.statement: Only the PM can create, delete, assign, move or re-baseline activities. An assignee can change only the % complete, actual start and actual finish of their own assigned activities. Entering % > 0 sets the actual start if blank; entering 100% sets the actual finish to today.
business_rules.applies_to: Activity, Activity Assignment / journeys J-03, J-04, J-11

business_rules.statement: S-curve points are computed weekly from project start to the later of baseline and forecast finish. Planned uses baseline dates; actual uses actual dates and % complete up to today; forecast runs from today to the forecast finish. All points are weighted by activity duration (BR-02). SPI = actual divided by planned, to date.
An issue escalates automatically when it is Critical, or when it passes its target resolution date by the configured aging period. Escalated issues appear on the PSC view and trigger notifications.
A risk escalates automatically when its rating is High or Critical. Escalated risks appear on the PSC view and trigger notifications.
Access to project data is restricted on a need-to-know basis and defaults to deny-all: a user sees and acts on only the projects they are explicitly assigned to.
business_rules.applies_to: Project, Project Assignment, User Account / journeys J-17 and every project-scoped PM/Team/DH/PS journey

business_rules.statement: A PSR moves Draft (PM, editable) -> Submitted -- For DH Review (locked) -> [Returned -> Draft] -> DH Approved -- For PS Approval (only when BR-10 applies) -> Approved (final, read-only snapshot; rolls into the PPSR and PSR history).
business_rules.applies_to: PSR / journeys J-08, J-09, J-12, J-13, J-15

business_rules.statement: A Department Head (or Project Sponsor) returning a PSR must provide comments explaining what needs to be corrected.

child_tables.name: Budget Changes

child_tables.rationale: Versioned baseline register (version, approval date, approver, budget at baseline) (J-02); the live baseline dates sit on each Activity.

child_tables.name: Decision Log
child_tables.rationale: Project decisions + rationale (J-05, ITPH-0038); simple log, optional reference to the Issue it resolves.

flows.rationale: Master record and reference hub for every other flow; status (Planning/Active/On Hold/Closed) is a master attribute, not a routed or board-moved workflow, and health indicators are computed (BR-02/03/05/06) from cross-flow aggregates. Form, not Board, because 8 flows reference it and PSC dashboards must list it (J-01, J-14).

flows.name: ITPMD Activity

child_tables.name: Predecessors
child_tables.rationale: Dependency rows (predecessor Activity ref, FS/SS/FF/SF, lag) owned by the successor activity (J-02, ITPH-006).

flows.rationale: Schedule line of record: planned/baseline/forecast/actual start+finish, % complete, planned duration (weight), responsible person, milestone flag. Status is DERIVED from % complete (BR-15), not user-moved, so Form not Board. Feeds Gantt, S-curve (BR-17), weighted % complete (BR-02), My Tasks (J-11).

flows.name: ITPMD Risk
flows.rationale: Risk register entry with computed 5x5 rating (BR-04) and computed escalation (BR-22); PM-maintained register, no routing. Form so PSC dashboards can list High/Critical risks directly (J-06, J-14).

flows.name: ITPMD Issue
flows.rationale: Ticket-shaped entity whose status (Open > In Progress > Resolved > Closed) is moved by the PM/owner with no fixed approval chain = Board per the Process-vs-Board rule; escalation (BR-21) is a computed flag, not a routing step (J-05, J-14).

flows.name: ITPMD Action Item
flows.rationale: To-do assigned to a team member and moved Open > Done by that assignee; must appear on the assignee's My Tasks across ALL projects (ITPH-00258) and can stand alone without an Issue, so it is its own Board, not a child table of Issue (J-05, J-11).

flows.name: ITPMD Cost Entry

child_tables.name: Invoices
child_tables.rationale: Vendor invoices (invoice/DO no+date, vendor, amount, date paid, status, remarks) billed against a cost/commitment line (J-07, ITPH-0057).

flows.rationale: Actual/committed/forecast cost lines per project, aggregated to Project for budget-vs-actual-vs-committed-vs-forecast and cost health (BR-05, J-07). PM-recorded data of record, no approval.

flows.name: ITPMD Project Status Report

child_tables.name: Schedule Highlights
child_tables.rationale: Activities/milestones behind, ahead, missed or forecast late (ITPH-0106..0108); rows reference Activity with autofilled dates/% = frozen snapshot (BR-13).

child_tables.name: Next Period Plan
child_tables.rationale: Activities/milestones planned for next period (ITPH-0104); rows reference Activity.

child_tables.name: Key Issues and Risks
child_tables.rationale: Issue/risk highlights for the reporting period, snapshotted onto the PSR.

flows.rationale: Core structured approval: Draft (PM) > DH Review > [conditional: PS Approval when BR-10] > Approved; Return = native send-back with mandatory comment (BR-24, BR-25). Header snapshots project health/financial/S-curve figures via Project lookup autofill so an approved PSR never changes (BR-13) (J-08, J-09, J-12, J-13).

flows.name: ITPMD Portfolio Status Report

child_tables.name: Project Summaries
child_tables.rationale: One row per approved PSR in the period (PSR ref + autofilled health/% complete/cost figures) = consolidated PPSR snapshot (ITPH-00101, BR-24).

flows.rationale: The PPSR as a persisted monthly artifact the PSC generates (J-15). No approval chain in the BRD, so Form. Live portfolio dashboards are separate derived pages (experience-designer).

flows.name: ITPMD Holiday Calendar
flows.rationale: Admin-maintained holidays / non-working days (J-16, BR-01). Dataform (the engine has no Dataset builder); consumed by working-day logic and the PSR deadline reminder automation.

flows.name: ITPMD Hub Settings
flows.rationale: Singleton-by-convention config record: PSR due working day, reminder offsets, issue aging period, escalation recipients (J-16, BR-11, BR-21). Dataform so thresholds change without a rebuild.

forms.name: ITPMD Issue

transitions.guard: BR-21: Priority = Critical, or Target_Resolution_Date passed by the configured aging period, while still Open
BR-21: Priority = Critical, or Target_Resolution_Date passed by the configured aging period, while still In Progress
PM/owner marks the escalated issue resolved
PM confirms closure (e.g. after related Action Items are Done)
Resolution rejected / issue recurs — reopened for further work

forms._workflow_notes: Issue is a Board (unstructured, user-moved) per D16 — the PM/owner drags cards; Open->Escalated and In Progress->Escalated are the one AUTOMATIC transition pair (BR-21/§6.3), fired by a scheduled check (kf-integration-analyst owns the actual automation) rather than a person's click. Every non-initial status reachable (In Progress, Escalated, Resolved, Closed); every non-terminal status has an outward move; Closed is the only terminal.

forms.name: ITPMD Action Item

transitions.guard: Due date has passed while still Open (ITPH-0037/00155)
Due date has passed while still In Progress (ITPH-0037/00155)
Assignee resumes work on a now-overdue item

forms._workflow_notes: Action Item is a Board, standalone from Issue per D16 (so it surfaces on each assignee's My Tasks across every project — ITPH-00258 — independent of any Issue). Overdue is reached automatically (a scheduled check against the due date), never dragged there by a person; every status has an outward move except the terminal Done, and every status is reachable from Open.

forms._workflow_notes: Assignee-per-record: Department Head Review and Sponsor Approval are performed by the role, but the SPECIFIC person is the one named on the PSR's own Department_Head / Project_Sponsor user fields (populated from the Project's DH/PS at PSR-creation time) — kf-security-designer should scope each role's process access to 'assigned records only' (BR-23) rather than 'all PSRs'. Project_Manager (user field) identifies the initiator/PM for notifications and My Items; the process actor role for Draft is Project Manager. Rejection/return is the native default (LESSONS-confirmed): no 'Returned' step is modeled — a Return decision on either approval step sends the item back to Draft with the platform's own mandatory-comment prompt, satisfying BR-25 without a second terminal.

permissions.intent: Coherence C1 (D26): Editable only so PSC portfolio-health charts on Portfolio Command Center pass NAV_GRANT_ESCALATION; live effect = Member+InitiateItems on PSR (same residual as DH/PS, SEC-1). No action card for PSC, so no +New surface; any PSC-raised PSR still routes through DH review. BRD 5.1 intent remains V.

itpmd_activity.note: Team Member edits limited by BR-15 to % complete/actual dates of their OWN assigned activity — see decision D-SEC-1 (field/row scoping is a residual gap, not enforced by the engine).

itpmd_psr.note: Department Head and Project Sponsor act on their own workflow steps (Editable) — per LESSONS §18 this also grants them InitiateItems; no narrower 'act-only' grant exists at the engine layer. Residual gap, documented not fabricated around. PSC Member is also declared Editable (D26/coherence C1) solely so its portfolio-health charts are gate-clean; this carries the same InitiateItems residual; no create affordance is surfaced to PSC.

scope_legend.my: records the user created, is assigned to (Responsible_Person / issue owner / action-item assignee / PM/DH/PS on the Project), or otherwise personally owns
scope_legend.my-team: records for projects where the user is the named Department Head or Project Sponsor (per-project user fields on ITPMD Project, not a role-wide grant)
scope_legend.all: every record in the flow, account-wide (portfolio-level oversight)

residual_gaps: BR-23 (deny-all per assigned project): the engine's permission entry grants view/edit on ALL items matching the coarse scope keyword (my/my-team/all); there is no native row-level 'only my assigned projects' filter. Mitigation: data-architect must build views/reports filtered by the per-project Department_Head/Project_Sponsor/Project Team fields (D21), and My Tasks/Project list views for PM/Team Member filtered to their own assignments — this is a VIEW-layer approximation of BR-23, not an engine-enforced ACL. A user with the URL/id of an unassigned project's record is not blocked by the platform itself.

BR-15 (assignee edits only % complete/actual dates of THEIR OWN activity): ITPMD Activity is a Form, so there is no per-step field_permissions mechanism (that only exists on Process/Case steps). Team Member is granted flow-level Editable, scope 'my' — this is all-or-nothing at the field level; a Team Member with edit access to their own activity row could technically also edit fields BR-15 reserves for the PM (WBS code, dates, dependencies, assignment). Mitigation: front-end/business validation (out of this agent's lane) must additionally gate which fields render editable per BR-15; the permission layer alone cannot express 'editable fields depend on whether this row is assigned to me'.

Department Head / Project Sponsor Editable on itpmd_psr (required so they can act on their approval step, LESSONS §18) also grants them InitiateItems — technically able to raise a new PSR themselves, not just review one. Accepted as a known platform limitation (no narrower process grant exists); mitigated at the experience layer by not surfacing a '+ New PSR' entry point to DH/PS pages (kf-experience-designer).

RG-PSC-PSR-INITIATE (D26): PSC Member holds InitiateItems on ITPMD Project Status Report (BRD 5.1 says V) because any page card on a Process for a ReadOnly role is gate-blocked; mitigated by no action card/+New for PSC and DH review of any PSR. Fix owner: engine (read-only card verb / flowGrant-aware NAV_GRANT_ESCALATION).

design.name: ITPMD Project Hub

type.mono: "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "JetBrains Mono", Menlo, monospace

design.rationale: Anchor: Ledger (`compact rows, stark numerals, raised cards and still motion. Ledgers, invoicing, treasury.`) was picked over runner-up Realty for a government bank's ITPM/PSR hub -- its dense-tabular, still-motion register fits schedules, budgets, invoices and monthly PSR approvals, and its IBM Plex Sans body font matches the BRD's mandated typeface (BRD §11.3) verbatim without needing an override. hueShift -53 deliberately exceeds the usual +/-40 guardrail: BRD §9.8 ITPH-00296 is a hard MVP requirement ('the system shall use the Bank's visual identity -- logo and green colour palette'), and the approved prototype's CSS pins exact hex values (primary #2F7D32, brand #74BC44, sidebar #123A1C). The shift was solved by inverting the anchor's own HSL math to land primary at hue 122 -- identical to #2F7D32's hue -- so the app reads as LANDBANK green, not generic teal, while keeping Ledger's font pairing, radius (0.75rem) and shadow/motion character untouched. Archetype rail-dark renders the prototype's dark-green navigation rail (BRD 'Sidebar green -- Navigation background') via the anchor's own dark-mode palette (sidebarDark 146 10% 8%, a near-black desaturated green close to #123A1C) rather than a hand-picked color. Density stays at Ledger's default 'compact' -- PSR schedules, risk registers and financial tables are dense grids that need to stay legible at the BRD's required tablet/phone widths without excess scroll.
